lines.cu1: A copper atom has twenty nine electrons, but only one sits in its outer shell.
lines.cu2: That lone electron is weakly bound, so it is easy to pull free.
lines.sea1: In solid copper, every atom shares its electron, forming a sea of free electrons.
lines.sea2: That is about one free electron per atom: a huge number of charge carriers.
lines.comp1: In rubber, electrons stay bound to their atoms, so nothing flows.
lines.comp2: In copper, electrons drift through a tidy lattice, with few collisions.
lines.rank1: Only silver beats it, but copper is cheaper, and easy to draw into wire.
lines.outro: Lots of free electrons, and an orderly lattice to flow through. That is why copper is a great conductor.
